# ETH-USD Technical Report (as of 2026-11-21)

ETH-USD is a crypto asset, so this analysis is technical only. No company fundamentals were used. All exact price and indicator values below come from the verified market snapshot unless stated otherwise.

## 1. Data integrity notes

- **The 2026-11-21 close differs between tools.** `get_stock_data` shows 1683.30 and the verified snapshot shows 1683.01. Open (1619.37), high (1706.36), low (1542.15) and volume (19,689,226,240) match. I use 1683.01.
- **Some indicator series differ slightly from the snapshot.** I use the snapshot values.

  | Indicator | `get_indicators` | Snapshot |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | 10 EMA | 1808.62 | 1808.66 |
  | 50 SMA | 2265.38 | 2265.39 |
  | RSI | 26.20 | 26.21 |
  | Bollinger lower band | 1537.22 | 1537.26 |

  The 200 SMA and ATR agree. The gaps are small, and the 11-21 bar may still be forming since crypto trades continuously. I can't confirm that cause.
- **The Bollinger middle and upper bands, MACD signal and MACD histogram come from the snapshot only.** I did not query separate time series for them, so I can't comment on their history.

## 2. Indicator selection and why

I chose eight complementary indicators:

- **Trend:** 10 EMA, 50 SMA and 200 SMA cover short-, medium- and long-term direction.
- **Momentum:** MACD (with its signal and histogram from the snapshot) and RSI.
- **Volatility and range:** Bollinger lower band (with the middle and upper bands from the snapshot) and ATR.
- **Volume:** VWMA.

## 3. Trend structure

**Price is below every moving average in the set.**

| Average | Value | Close vs. average |
|---|---:|---:|
| 10 EMA | 1808.66 | about -6.9% |
| VWMA | 1860.64 | below |
| Bollinger middle (20) | 2001.60 | below |
| 200 SMA | 2125.42 | about -20.8% |
| 50 SMA | 2265.39 | about -25.7% |

- **The short-term trend is down.** The 10 EMA has fallen almost every day across the 30-day window, from 2442.07 on 10-22 to 1808.62 on 11-21.
- **The 50 SMA is falling, from 2550.90 on 10-22 to 2265.38.** It is still above the 200 SMA (2125.42) by about 140 points, so no death cross has occurred yet.
- **The gap between the 50 and 200 SMAs is closing fast.** It was about 396 points on 10-22. A bearish crossover is a plausible near-term development to watch. Projecting a date from that pace would be an extrapolation, not a signal.
- **The 200 SMA is nearly flat**, at 2154.66 on 10-22 and 2125.42 now. The long-term benchmark has not yet turned down, but price is far beneath it.
- **VWMA at 1860.64 sits above price.** Volume-weighted average prices are higher than the current price, so recent heavy-volume trading happened at higher levels. That is consistent with the sell-off, and holders from those levels are underwater.

## 4. Price action context (from the OHLCV data)

- **Breakout and full retracement.** ETH-USD closed 1916.46 on 08-18, then 2251.46 on 08-19 (high 2327.70, volume about 29.6B). It peaked at a 2776.47 close on 09-21 (intraday high 2805.50). The current close is about 39% below that peak. It is also below the pre-breakout range of closes around 1871–1916 from 08-10 to 08-18, so the whole advance has been given back.
- **Failed rally on 11-04.** Price closed 2422.31 on 11-04 (high 2446.05), then closed 2234.48 on 11-05, a drop of about 7.8%. Supply around 2400–2450 absorbed that bounce.
- **Accelerating decline.** Closes went 2016.83 (11-12), 1927.59 (11-13) and 1769.12 (11-14). After a brief bounce, 11-20 closed at 1619.43, down about 7.7% on the day on the highest volume (21.48B) since 09-21 in this dataset.
- **11-21 is a rebound candle.** It opened at 1619.37, dipped to 1542.15, and closed at 1683.01 (about +3.9% from 11-20), near the upper part of its 1542.15–1706.36 range. The long lower wick shows buyers stepped in near the lows. One bar, possibly still forming, does not confirm a reversal.

## 5. Momentum

- **MACD is bearish and deepening.** MACD is -171.60, below its signal of -145.76, with a histogram of -25.84. The MACD line was -54.31 on 11-04 and -108.72 on 11-13. Its daily change slowed on 11-21 (-169.28 to -171.60), but that is one bar helped by the bounce.
- **RSI is oversold at 26.21, but not on a single day.** It has been below 30 every day from 11-12 through 11-21 (10 consecutive readings). It touched 19.80 on 11-14 and 19.54 on 11-20. In a trending decline, RSI can stay depressed, so oversold alone is not a buy signal.
- **No bullish RSI divergence yet.** The 11-20 close (1619.43) is far below the 11-14 close (1769.12), while RSI made only a marginally lower low (19.54 vs 19.80). Price and RSI confirm each other, so there is no divergence setup.

## 6. Volatility and risk

- **Bollinger Bands:**
  - The lower band is 1537.26, the middle is 2001.60 and the upper is 2465.93.
  - The 11-21 intraday low (1542.15) came within about 5 points of the lower band without piercing it.
  - The close at 1683.01 sits roughly 16% of the way from the lower to the upper band.
  - The bands are wide, about 46% of the middle line, reflecting expanded volatility. The lower band has fallen from 2281.38 on 10-22.
  - In strong downtrends, price can ride the lower band, so a touch is not a reversal signal by itself.
- **ATR is 110.22**, up from 78.86 on 11-03 and about 6.5% of the current price. This is high volatility for sizing and stops. A 1.5–2× ATR stop distance is roughly 165–220 points (about 10–13% of price). Position sizes should be reduced accordingly.

## 7. Key levels from the tool data

These are reference levels from the data, not validated support or resistance.

**Downside**
- 1537.26 (Bollinger lower band).
- 1542.15 (the 11-21 intraday low).
- Prior swing lows from earlier in the data: 1506.51 on 06-06 and 1510.51 on 06-26. Price closed 1686.40 on 06-07 and 1698.17 on 07-02, so it did rebound after those lows, though that is only two observations.

**Upside**
- 1755.19 (11-19 close) and 1769.12 (11-14 close).
- 1808.66 (10 EMA).
- 1860.64 (VWMA).
- 1927.59 (11-13 close).
- 2001.60 (Bollinger middle).
- 2125.42 (200 SMA).
- 2265.39 (50 SMA).

## 8. Scenarios

- **Bearish continuation (currently favored by trend and momentum):**
  - Price stays under the 10 EMA and VWMA, MACD stays below its signal, and a daily close below about 1537 follows.
  - The 1506–1511 prior-lows zone would then be the next reference.
  - Watch for the 50/200 SMA cross.
- **Relief bounce:**
  - Oversold RSI, a lower-band touch and a rejection wick on heavy volume make a counter-trend bounce plausible.
  - Initial hurdles are 1755–1770 and then the 10 EMA at about 1809.
  - A bounce into falling averages would remain within the downtrend unless price reclaims the VWMA (about 1861) and the 11-13 close (1927.59).
- **Neutral or unconfirmed:** a hold above 1542 for several sessions, with RSI rising back above 30 and the MACD histogram shrinking, would be the first sign of stabilization. None of that is present yet.

## 9. Summary

The trend is clearly bearish across all timeframes, with oversold readings and a rebound candle at the Bollinger lower band as the main counter-signals. The data supports a cautious or defensive stance rather than treating oversold RSI as a buy signal. Any long idea would be a counter-trend trade needing tight, ATR-based risk control, and any short idea faces squeeze risk from oversold conditions. The final trading decision is left to the next agent.

What the bull got right: 11-20 looked like capitulation (down 7.7% on 21.48B of volume, the highest since September). 11-21 rejected the lower Bollinger band at 1537, with a low of 1542 and a close of 1683. RSI hit 19.5, price is about 21% below the 200 SMA, and price is sitting on the 1506-1510 zone that held twice in June. He correctly noted that no death cross has occurred and that a 90%-priced hike is not new information. Proposing a defined stop was sensible discipline.

Why the bear's case decided it:
(1) The reversal is one unfinished candle. ETH trades 24/7 and the two sources disagree on the 11-21 close (1683.30 vs 1683.01), so the bar is likely still printing. There is no higher low. The bull's own confirmation signals (RSI above 30, a shrinking MACD histogram, holding above 1542) are all missing, and he wants to buy before them. That is the weakest point in his case.
(2) The only probability evidence points toward the stop. Prediction markets give 58% for touching $1,500 (up 12.7pp this week), slightly below the 1506 stop, plus 28% for $1,250 and 12% for $1,000, with upside odds near zero. A 2.5:1 trade needs about a 29% chance of reaching 2125 before 1506, and nothing in the data supports that. The bull never answered when the bear asked him to.
(3) The path to the target is crowded: 1716.6 (the bearish break of structure), 1755-1769, the 10 EMA at 1809, the VWMA at 1861, 1927 and the Bollinger middle at 2001. A VWMA above price means heavy-volume buyers are underwater and likely to sell into rallies.
(4) The averages are falling toward price. The 50 SMA dropped from 2551 to 2265 in 30 days and the 50/200 gap shrank from about 396 to about 140 points, so mean reversion can happen by the mean coming down.
(5) The stop is too tight for current volatility. ATR is 110 (about 6.5% of price), so 1506 is only about 1.6 ATR away, and one or two ordinary down days would hit it.
